subject: OpenForge publishing ops: access, escrow, and legal checklist
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@openforge.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential publisher bundle — access & distribution ops

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the intro at the conference last week — we appreciated the booth walkthrough. OpenForge Labs is preparing a small suite of open-weight models (2 variants: base and instruction-tuned) that we want to make broadly accessible via partner catalogs. Before we get too deep, can you outline Redwood's operational and legal expectations for:

- Weights hosting / escrow (do you require an escrow copy or only a signed checksum?)
- Allowed quantization / derivative builds (we plan to publish float32 + integer quantized variants)
- Attribution and display requirements (UI/marketing language)
- Revenue share or referral options for bundled ISV distributions

Attached is a short model spec and a draft publisher one-pager. We'd like to run this through a quick ops + legal checklist and, if all aligned, kick off a technical onboarding sandbox next week.

Samir
Co-founder, OpenForge Labs
partners@openforge.ai

Attachments: OpenForge_Model_Specs_v1.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@openforge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential publisher bundle — access & distribution ops

Hi Samir — great to meet you in person. Looping in Marcus (partnerships ops) and Naomi (publisher go-to-market) to own the program details and legal/contract questions. High-level answers below so we can get a scoped list before we involve security/legal counsel formally: 

- Escrow: Redwood prefers that publishers either (A) deposit an escrow copy with a neutral third-party escrow (we can recommend providers), or (B) provide a signed SHA256 checksum + manifest and transfer rights via DocuSign. For narrow regulatory customers we often require escrow.
- Quantization/derivatives: We support multiple quantization formats. We generally ask publishers to tag each artifact with an explicit license and quantization metadata (e.g., q4_0, int8-sym). If a publisher wants to restrict certain derivative builds, that needs to be explicit in the publisher agreement.
- Attribution: Standard attribution line in UI + model card is acceptable: "Model: OpenForge Labs / OF-Large-v1 (license)"
